1.explanation:
1. src/table/util.js – this is where fetchDataByPath lives. It turns dataIndex into a string, splits on dots and only handles a single bracket expression (/(.*)\[(.*)\]/). It never parses full array syntax or an actual JS array, so dataIndex="['range','start','end']" falls through and returns undefined. 
2. types/table/index.d.ts – the Table.Column dataIndex prop is only typed as string; if we want to accept string[] or a literal array, the TypeScript definitions need to be updated accordingly. Together, these two files must be changed so that fetchDataByPath will detect an Array or a JSON array string, iterate each path segment, and return the nested values as intended, and the types will allow passing dataIndex as an array of keys.
1.bug_scenario: In the Table component a column’s dataIndex was written as the literal string "['range','start','end']" in order to map two nested values in the record (range.start and range.end). The current fetchDataByPath utility only supports dot-notation (a.b.c) and a single simple bracket lookup (e.g. "list[0]"). As a result, when it sees the JSON-like string '["range","start","end"]', it returns undefined, and downstream code throws “Cannot read property ‘startDate,endDate’ of undefined” at render time.

2.explanation: The root of the problem lives in src/table/util.js in the fetchDataByPath function. That function currently only supports dot-separated paths and a single key[index] pattern, but it never parses a full bracket-notation string as an array of keys. When you pass "['range','start','end']" as dataIndex, path.toString() yields "['range','start','end']", split('.') yields one entry, field[0] includes the brackets, and the existing regex match only extracts two groups, so you never drill down properly into object.range.start.end. To fix this bug, you must update fetchDataByPath (src/table/util.js) to detect and parse bracket-notation strings (e.g. JSON-parse them into an array of keys, or run a loop over multiple bracket matches) and then iterate through each key in turn.
2.bug_scenario: In the Table component, when you pass a dataIndex value in the form of a bracket‐notation string – for example "['range','start','end']" – the table’s internal fetchDataByPath function doesn’t recognize it. It simply calls path.toString(), splits on '.', and then only handles a single [key] lookup pattern. As a result, fetchDataByPath returns undefined for nested bracket paths, and the cell renderer later does something like undefined.startDate and blows up with a TypeError.
